# Introduction

Peaks were called using macs2 [@feng2012identifying] within the NFCore/ATAC pipeline [@harshil_patel_2023_8222875] using the default filters and parameters. The following sections provide an overview of the number of peaks called, their reproducibility across replicates, and the quality control metrics associated with the peak calling process.

```{r setup,include=F,echo=FALSE}
options(bitmapType='cairo')
```


```{r source-global-script,warning=F,include=F}
source("code/globalfun.R")
```



```{r read-in-sample-sheet}
sample.sheet<-readRDS("output/sample_sheet.valid.rds")
sample.sheet$group<-gsub("_REP.*","",sample.sheet$sample)
```

```{r load-multiqc-data}
load("output/processed_data.RData")
```



```{r specify-peak-caller-peak-location}
peakcaller = list("macs2" = "narrowPeak")
path2peaks <- "output/NFCore_ATACseq//bwa/merged_library/macs2/narrow_peak/"
```

```{r get-number-of-peaks, eval=FALSE}
peakN = c()
peakWidth = c()
for (samp in gsub("_T1", "", sample.sheet$sample)) {
  for (caller in names(peakcaller)) {
    peakInfo = read.table(
      paste0(path2peaks, "/",samp,".mLb.clN_peaks.narrowPeak"),
      header = FALSE,
      fill = TRUE
    )  %>% mutate(width = abs(V3 - V2))
    peakN = data.frame(
      peakN = nrow(peakInfo),
      Caller = caller,
      Group = gsub("_R.*", "", samp),
      Sample = samp,
      Replicate = gsub(".*_", "", samp)
    ) %>% rbind(peakN, .)
    peakWidth = data.frame(
      width = peakInfo$width,
      Group = gsub("_R.*", "", samp),
      Sample = samp,
      Replicate = gsub(".*_", "", samp)
    )  %>% rbind(peakWidth, .)
  }
}
save(peakN,peakWidth, file = "output/peak_counts.RData")
```

\FloatBarrier

# Exploration of peak calls

Here the number of peaks together with their reproducibility across replicates are explored. The reproducibility score for each group is calculated based on the consistency of peak detection across its corresponding replicate samples. Specifically, it measures the proportion of peaks that overlap (i.e., are found in similar locations or regions) among the replicates within that group, relative to the total number of peaks considered. Higher percentages indicate greater consistency between replicates for that group.


## Number of peaks called

```{r load-peak-counts}
load("output/peak_counts.RData")
generate_datatable(
  peakN[,c("Sample","Group","peakN")],
  caption = "Total number of peaks per replicate",extra.options = NULL
)
```
\FloatBarrier

The Barplot below represents the total number of peaks identified in each library.

```{r bar-num-peaks, fig.cap="Number of peaks called for each library", fig.width=10,fig.height=8}
ggplot(peakN, aes(
  x = Sample, y = peakN,fill=Group)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(1)) +
  coord_flip() + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(
    scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) +
  theme_minimal() +  
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(peakN/1000,"k")),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    size = 3
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1
    ),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )
```

\FloatBarrier

## Sample Peak reproducibility

The bar plot below displays the percentage of peak reproducibility for different sample groups. The reproducibility score for each group is calculated based on the consistency of peak detection across its corresponding replicate samples. Specifically, it measures the proportion of peaks that overlap (i.e., are found in similar locations or regions) among the replicates within that group, relative to the total number of peaks considered. Higher percentages indicate greater consistency between replicates for that group.

```{r get-sample-peak-reproducibility, eval=FALSE}
library(GenomicRanges)
samples <- unique(sample.sheet$group)
peakOverlap_df_list <- list()
peakOverlap.list <- list()

for (caller in names(peakcaller)) {
  # Initialize the nested list for this specific caller to prevent subscript errors
  peakOverlap.list[[caller]] <- list() 
  
  for (samp in samples) {
    # Extract replicates for the current group
    repL <- gsub("_T1", "", sample.sheet$sample[sample.sheet$group == samp])
        gr_list <- list()
    
    for (repl in repL) {
      file_path <- file.path(path2peaks, paste0(repl, ".mLb.clN_peaks.narrowPeak"))
      
      peakInfo <- read.table(file_path, header = FALSE, fill = TRUE)
      
      gr_list[[repl]] <- GRanges(
        seqnames = peakInfo$V1,
        ranges = IRanges(start = peakInfo$V2, end = peakInfo$V3),
        strand = "*"
      )
    }
    if (length(gr_list) > 0) {
      overlap.gr <- Reduce(subsetByOverlaps, gr_list)
    } else {
      overlap.gr <- GRanges()
    }
    
    # Store the overlapping GRanges object
    peakOverlap.list[[caller]][[samp]] <- overlap.gr
    
    # Store the metrics as a single-row dataframe in our list
    list_name <- paste(caller, samp, sep = "_")
    peakOverlap_df_list[[list_name]] <- data.frame(
      Group = samp,
      Caller = caller,
      peakReprod = length(overlap.gr)
    )
  }
}

peakOverlap <- bind_rows(peakOverlap_df_list)

peakReprod <- left_join(peakN, peakOverlap, by = c("Group", "Caller")) %>% 
  mutate(peakReprodRate = (peakReprod / peakN) * 100)

# 5. Final Selection
final_metrics <- peakReprod %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    Group,
    Caller,
    Replicate, # Assuming this exists in your original peakN dataframe
    peakN,
    peakReprodNum = peakReprod,
    peakReprodRate
  )
save(peakReprod,file="output/peakReprod.RData")
```

\FloatBarrier

```{r peak-reproducibility-plot,fig.cap="Percentage of sample peak reproducibility calculated from the total number of overlapping peaks within group replicate sets",fig.width=10,fig.height=8}
load("output/peakReprod.RData")
ggplot(peakReprod, aes(
  x = Sample, y = peakReprodRate,fill=Group)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(1)) +
  coord_flip() + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(
    scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) +
  labs(title = "Peak reproducibility %",
       x = "Sample",
       y = "Reproducibility (%)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1
    ),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )
```

## Number of concensus peaks per condition

The bar plot below represents the total number of concensus peaks identified in each condition. Concensus peaks are defined as those that are consistently detected across all replicates within a given condition, providing a more reliable representation of the underlying biological signal.

```{r number-concensus-peaks,fig.height=8,fig.width=18, fig.cap="Number of concensus peaks per condition"}
plot_data <- data.frame(
  Sample = rownames(peak_count.stats_conc),
  Peak_count = diag(peak_count.stats_conc)
)
ggplot(plot_data,
       aes(x = Sample, y = Peak_count,fill = Sample)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "",
       x = "",
       y = "Peak count") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Peak_count / 1000, 2), "k")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            size = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 14
    ),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )
```

## Fraction of Reads in Peaks (FRiP) score

The Fraction of Reads in Peaks (FRiP) score is a quality metric that quantifies the proportion of sequencing reads that fall within the called peak regions. A higher FRiP score indicates better enrichment of signal over background noise, suggesting that the peak calling was effective and that the data is of high quality. In general, a FRiP score above 1% is considered acceptable for ATAC-seq data, with higher values indicating better quality.

### Per library

```{r get-FRiP-per-library}
peak.qual$group <-gsub("_REP.*","",peak.qual$Sample)
colnames(peak.qual)[ncol(peak.qual)-1]<-"FRiP"
```

```{r plot-FRiP-library,fig.height=6,fig.width=12, fig.cap="Fraction of Reads in Peaks called per library"}
ggplot(peak.qual, aes(
  x = Sample, y = FRiP,fill=group)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() + 
  labs(title = "FRiP",
       x = "",
       y = "FRiP",
       fill= "group") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(FRiP,"%")),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    size = 3
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 14
    ),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )
```

# Peak annotation

Called peaks were annotated using Homer within the NFCore/ATAC pipeline [@harshil_patel_2023_8222875]. The figures below represent the number of peaks annotated to different genomic features per library and per condition. The annotation provides insights into the genomic context of the identified peaks, helping to understand their potential regulatory roles.

## Transcription Start Site (TSS) enrichment plot and heatmap

The following figures represent the Transcription Start Site (TSS) enrichment plot and heatmap, which provide insights into the distribution of sequencing reads around TSS regions. These visualizations help assess the quality of the ATAC-seq data by indicating how well the reads are enriched at TSS regions, which is a hallmark of open chromatin and active regulatory elements.

```{r stitch-pdfs, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=12}
library(magick)
library(cowplot)
enrich.plots<-"docs/figure/enrichplot_heatmap/"
pdf_files <- list.files(path = enrich.plots,
                        pattern = "\\.pdf$",
                        full.names = TRUE)

plot_list <- lapply(pdf_files, function(p) {
  ggdraw() + draw_image(image_read_pdf(p, density = 300))
})
plot_grid(plotlist = plot_list, ncol = 7)
```


```{r download-enrichment-plots}
include_dir_download(enrich.plots,"TSS-enrichment-heatmap-plots")
```

# Appendix

## ATACqv Report

The ATACqv [@orchard2020quantification] report provides a comprehensive overview of the quality control metrics for the ATAC-seq data. It includes various plots and tables that summarize the quality of the sequencing data, including metrics such as read depth, fragment size distribution, and peak calling statistics. The report is generated using the ATACqv tool, which is specifically designed for assessing the quality of ATAC-seq experiments.

```{r embed-atacqv-report, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_url("ataqv/narrow_peak/html/index.html", height = "800px")
```

## All Code used in this analysis

This section provides a comprehensive overview of all the R code chunks used throughout this analysis. It serves as a reference for reproducibility and transparency, allowing readers to understand the specific steps and functions employed in the data processing and analysis.

```{r appendix, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# Get all chunk labels in the document
labels <- knitr::all_labels()

# Exclude this specific chunk so it doesn't print its own generation code
labels <- labels[labels != "appendix"]

# Loop through each label, print a markdown header, and then the code block
for (label in labels) {
  # Print the header (you can change the #### to adjust the heading size)
  cat("#### Chunk: `", label, "`\n\n", sep = "")
  
  # Print the opening of the code block
  cat("```r\n")
  
  # Fetch and print the actual code from the chunk
  cat(knitr::knit_code$get(label), sep = "\n")
  
  # Print the closing of the code block
  cat("\n```\n\n")
}
```
